overview.text:
Amritsar grew from the settlement Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru, founded in 1574 around the Amrit Sarovar, the pool of nectar that gives the city its name. At its centre is the Golden Temple, the holiest site of Sikhism, its upper storey covered in almost 400 kg of gold leaf. Its langar serves about 100,000 free vegetarian meals a day to anyone who comes.

A short walk away are Jallianwala Bagh and the Partition Museum, and more historic gurdwaras, Gobindgarh Fort and the gold-domed Durgiana Temple are close by. Every evening before sunset, the Beating Retreat ceremony is held at the Attari–Wagah border, about 28–30 km west. Food is a reason to come in itself: Amritsari kulcha, poori chholey, dhaba dal and lassi. October to March is the most pleasant time to visit.

items.title: How far is the Wagah border from Amritsar?
items.body: About 28–30 km west, on the Grand Trunk Road.

items.title: Is the langar really free?
items.body: Yes. It serves free vegetarian meals to everyone, day and night.

items.title: When is the best time to visit?
items.body: October to March. Summers can reach 45 °C.

items.title: Can I attend the Wagah ceremony?
items.body: Yes. The UK government advises against travel within 10 km of the border except at the Wagah–Attari crossing, and says visitors can still attend the daily retreat ceremony, though the crossing itself is closed. Check your own government's current advice.

faqs.q: When is the Golden Temple best?
faqs.a: Early morning for calm, and at night when it is lit up. For the sanctum queue, late afternoon and early evening are suggested.

faqs.q: How long does the Wagah trip take?
faqs.a: Half a day including about 28–30 km each way.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay for langar?
faqs.a: No, it is free to all.
